text:
Predicates:
GivenOnTV(x, y, z) ::: x is given out on TV on y at z.
Rose(x) ::: x is a rose.
Bachelor(x) ::: x is on the Bachelor.
PortraysRealLives(x) ::: x portrays the lives of real people.
RealityTV(x) ::: x is a reality TV show.
Premises:
∃x ∃y (Monday(y) ∧ Time(y, 8pm) ∧ Rose(x) ∧ GivenOnTV(x, TV, y)) ::: On some Mondays at 8 pm, roses are given out on TV.
∀x (Rose(x) ∧ GivenOnTV(x, TV, y) → Bachelor(x)) ::: Every rose given out on TV is on the Bachelor.
∀x (Bachelor(x) → PortraysRealLives(x)) ::: Everything on the Bachelor portrays the lives of real people.
∀x (PortraysRealLives(x) → RealityTV(x)) ::: All shows portraying the lives of real people are reality TV shows.
¬RealityTV(breakingBad) ::: Breaking Bad is not a reality TV show.
Conclusion:
∀x ∃y (Rose(x) ∧ GivenOnTV(x, breakingBad, y) → (Monday(y) ∧ Time(y, 8pm))) ::: If roses are given out during Breaking Bad, then it is on Monday at 8 pm.
